final_message:
I implemented `slugify` in `labkit/util/text.py`, and `python3 -m unittest tests.test_o1_slugify` passes (1 test, OK).

It works in four steps:
1. It decomposes the title with Unicode NFKD normalization and drops the combining accent marks, so "Café" becomes "Cafe".
2. It lower-cases the result.
3. It replaces every run of characters other than `a-z` and `0-9` with a single `-`.
4. It strips `-` from both ends.

The one test covers four cases: punctuation, accents with extra spaces, an all-dash input that gives an empty string, and mixed letters and digits. I didn't test other inputs.

     digits, replace every run of other characters with a single "-", and trim
     "-" from both ends.
     """
-    raise NotImplementedError
+    import re
+    import unicodedata
+
+    decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", title)
+    ascii_text = "".join(c for c in decomposed if not unicodedata.combining(c))
+    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", ascii_text.lower()).strip("-")
